key_insight: This paper introduces Camera-controllable Video Virtual Try-on (CaM-VVT), enabling realistic virtual try-on video synthesis from new, user-chosen viewpoints instead of being locked to the original camera path. The key idea is a renderable 4D try-on proxy that makes viewpoint exploration interactive and more flexible.
problem_solved: Existing video virtual try-on methods can only follow the source video’s camera trajectory, which limits users from freely changing viewpoints and prevents omnidirectional exploration of the dressed subject.
method: Defines CaM-VVT as a new task for camera-controllable try-on video generation.
Builds a renderable 4D try-on proxy to represent the person-garment scene in a viewable, controllable form.
Uses the proxy to synthesize try-on results under arbitrary camera trajectories while preserving garment realism and motion consistency.
impact: This work expands virtual try-on from passive video editing to interactive viewpoint control, which is valuable for e-commerce, AR/VR, and digital fashion. For practitioners, it points toward more generalizable video generation systems that separate appearance modeling from camera motion.
visual_elements: A before/after comparison of standard VVT vs. camera-controllable VVT.
A 4D proxy pipeline diagram showing source video -> proxy -> new camera path -> output video.
An orbit-style viewpoint graphic illustrating omnidirectional exploration around the subject.
An example grid of the same outfit rendered from multiple camera angles.
paper_title: TryOnCrafter: Unleashing Camera Trajectories for Realistic Video Virtual Try-on via a Renderable 4D Try-on Proxy
paper_authors: Hao Sun, Hao Yan, Mengting Chen, Quanjian Song, Yu Li
